sources.title: Ivan Cherednik, Lectures on the affine Hecke algebras and Macdonald conjectures, Harvard lectures (1994)
sources.locator: Lecture 3, §§3.8–3.13, PDF pp. 18–20; the complete surrounding presentation and polynomial representation were inspected.

contents.name: Lemma 3.10, Bernstein–Lusztig relation and polynomial divisibility
contents.support: Confirms the swapped-variable divided difference and that its numerator is divisible in the Laurent group algebra; the item proves the all-integer-exponent geometric-sum argument locally.

contents.name: Definition of the affine Hecke algebra and Lemma 3.10
contents.support: Supplies the affine Hecke and Bernstein relation interface in root-data notation; local proof fixes the universal Q normalization and checks the generator equivalence.

contents.name: Theorem 3.11, Bernstein ordered basis
contents.support: States the ordered Bernstein basis. The source defers its independence proof to Humphreys, Chapter 7; this batch supplies the full local spanning, leading-term independence, and arbitrary-base-change arguments.

contents.name: Theorem 3.12, center
contents.support: States the Weyl-invariant Laurent center. The source uses a specialization argument for the reverse inclusion; this batch proves the universal-ring statement directly.

contents.name: Theorem 3.13, polynomial representation
contents.support: Provides the polynomial representation interface. This batch verifies quadratic, distant, and adjacent braid relations by a complete six-permutation coefficient calculation.

sources.title: I. G. Macdonald, Affine Hecke algebras and orthogonal polynomials, Séminaire Bourbaki 797, Astérisque 237 (1996)
sources.locator: §4.1–4.6, PDF pp. 8–10 (printed Astérisque pp. 196–198); the complete 20-page scan and the full relevant section were inspected.

contents.name: §4.2, Bernstein–Lusztig relation and Laurent polynomial divisibility
contents.support: Supports the quotient relation and its Laurent-polynomial character; local proof treats negative exponent differences explicitly.

contents.name: §4.1–4.2, affine Hecke presentation and finite normalization
contents.support: Confirms the multiplicative Hecke normalization and Bernstein relation in the root-datum setting.

contents.name: §4.3, Bernstein ordered basis
contents.support: States the two ordered bases; the cited source refers elsewhere for the finite Hecke basis and does not give the universal Laurent leading-term proof used here.

contents.name: §4.5, invariant center
contents.support: Gives the invariant-center statement and a specialization route for the reverse inclusion; local proof does not use that route.

contents.name: §4.6, basic rational-function representation
contents.support: Supports the rational-function polynomial representation; all operator relations needed for this item are checked locally.

sources.title: Eric Opdam and Maarten Solleveld, Homological algebra for affine Hecke algebras (2007)
sources.locator: §1.2, PDF pp. 10–11, Theorem 1.3(a)–(c); the complete 55-page article and the full relevant subsection were inspected.

contents.name: Theorem 1.3(a), Bernstein bases
contents.support: Independent general-root-data statement of both ordered bases; it cites Bernstein/Lusztig for the theorem, so the local proof remains the source of this batch's derivation.

contents.name: Theorem 1.3(c), invariant center
contents.support: Independent statement of the invariant center in the complex root-data setting; local proof establishes the universal integral parameter version.

sources.title: George Lusztig, Lectures on Hecke Algebras with Unequal Parameters, MIT lecture notes, arXiv:math/0108172
sources.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 8–9; Proposition 3.3 and its proof were read in full.

contents.name: Proposition 3.3, generic Hecke standard basis
contents.support: The source proves the standard basis over the one-parameter Laurent ring; the local lemma makes the Q=v² normalization and the free rank-two descent to Z[Q,Q^-1] explicit.

sources.title: Anders Björner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups, Springer GTM 231 (2005), complete author-hosted book
sources.locator: §6.1, printed pp. 174–175 (PDF pp. 182–183), finite Hecke normalization and standard-basis summary.

contents.name: §6.1, finite Hecke basis and normalization
contents.support: Independent book treatment of the finite standard basis in square-root normalization; the local proof supplies the specific universal Q descent.

sources.title: Gaston Burrull, Notes on the Bernstein Presentation of the Hecke Algebra, supervisor Geordie Williamson
sources.locator: §1.1 and §2.5, PDF pp. 1–5: Iwahori–Matsumoto convolution motivation and Bernstein's algebraic presentation; the complete seven-page note was inspected.

contents.name: §1.1, Iwahori–Matsumoto convolution construction and algebraic Bernstein construction
contents.support: Used only for the page's scope comparison: convolution requires a p-adic group and Iwahori subgroup, while the present page defines an algebraic presentation. The note itself calls its exposition rough; no proof supplier is taken from it.
contents.reason: This source passage compares p-adic Iwahori convolution with algebraic Bernstein presentations. The present pair works over its universal Laurent coefficient ring and does not construct a p-adic group, Iwahori subgroup, or convolution algebra. It is page-level scope context, absorbed by no item proof; no mathematical result of this pair is removed.

sources.title: Ivan Cherednik, Lectures on the affine Hecke algebras and Macdonald conjectures, Harvard lectures (1994)
sources.locator: Lecture3, Lemma3.10 and Theorems3.12–3.13, printed pp.19–20: Laurent divisibility, invariant center and polynomial action.

contents.name: Lecture3: Bernstein relation and Laurent-polynomial divisibility
contents.support: The general Laurent divided-difference construction is specialized through the proved local A definition. The selected monomial X1^-2 X2 and its three-term quotient are original local data, verified by multiplying by 1-X1/X2; the rank-two generator computation is also local.

contents.name: Lecture3: polynomial representation
contents.support: The general source polynomial-representation formula supports the local A operator, whose full relations are proved locally in universal multiplicative Q normalization. The B proof substitutes 1,X1,X2 and computes Q,X2,QX1+(Q-1)X2; these exact evaluations are not attributed to the source.

contents.name: Lecture3: invariant Laurent center
contents.support: Source states the center as Weyl-invariant Laurent polynomials in its own coefficient setting. B uses the independently proved universal local theorem to show elementary symmetric polynomials central and X1 noncentral. No source proof or arbitrary-specialization center claim is substituted for that theorem.

sources.reading_verification: Read the complete relevant pp.19–20 from the retained full 42-page source.
